description: Changes data (adds bills); needs sign-in. To explain a bill or a month-on-month increase, use explain_bill. Record what the user actually paid each service in a month, on one of their saved stacks or audits, and compare it with the estimate at the users it was saved with. Without id, the bills are kept on the account, not on a stack (for someone who has not saved one): they are recorded and listed, with no estimate to compare, and can be moved onto a stack later on the Billing page. Pass bills (month as YYYY-MM, the service as vendor_id or name as on the invoice, amount_usd), or csv: a billing export with columns for month or date, service or vendor, and amount, or invoice_text: an invoice's text as pasted from the PDF or email (the service, month and total are read from it, each with the invoice line it came from; preview: true reads it without saving, so the user can check it first). A bill replaces any earlier one for the same service and month; remove deletes a month (or one service in it). Returns, per service, the estimate, the bill and the difference, flagging bills more than 20% (and $5) over or under. With alerts on, a bill well over its estimate is emailed too. Needs sign-in. How to present: a table of service, estimate, billed and difference; then say what could explain the biggest gap (more users or usage than given, a plan above the one assumed, add-ons the catalogue does not price) and offer update_saved_stack with the real user count.

amount_usd.description: Dollars, as a number or text such as "$1,204.50".

csv.description: A CSV billing export: a header row, then one row per charge.

id.description: The saved stack or audit. Leave out to keep the bills on the account.

invoice_text.description: One invoice's text, copied from the PDF or the email.

month.description: Which month to compare. Default: the newest with bills.

preview.description: With invoice_text: read it and show what was found, without saving.

vendor.description: vendor_id or name; leave out to remove the whole month.

name: record_bills

assumptions.description: Usage and pricing assumptions behind the numbers.

caveats.description: Show to the user word for word.

completeness.description: On plan and project results: complete, complete_with_assumptions, incomplete or needs_clarification, with the reasons. Say plainly when it is not complete.

data.description: The tool result. Its shape depends on the tool.

disclosures.description: Always includes the neutrality note: no vendor pays for a place in the answer. Link its url when you mention how Kong Reviews is paid.

project.description: On results about a saved project: its id and the context version the answer was computed on. Pass both back in follow-up calls.

title: Record what a stack or account actually cost
